steps.title: Build the invariant Claim Ladder brief
steps.prompt_exact: Can you build a self-contained one-file HTML game called First-Principles Claim Ladder where I test a big plan by moving claim, assumption, evidence, and experiment cards up a ladder, score whether the plan holds or collapses, and copy or download a reasoning receipt I can keep offline?
steps.response_exact:
Correcting a filename typo in that share — here's the actual file:Done. Single file, fully offline, scanner-verified clean on all seven constraints (no innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML, no inline handlers, no alert/confirm/prompt, no URL literals or external deps, no letter-spacing, no vw/clamp, and no localStorage) plus a `node --check` pass on the JS.

How the game works:

**Setup** — Type your big plan and lock it. Then forge cards in one of four types: Claim, Assumption, Evidence, Experiment. Any card can be flagged **load-bearing**.

**The ladder** — All cards start in the Deck. Four rungs above it: Stated → Stress-tested → Evidenced → Verified. Climbing a rung requires answering that rung's challenge inline (falsifiable restatement, steelman objection, concrete observation, kill-condition test) with a 20-character minimum. Answers get logged to the card. You can demote cards back down.

**Scoring** — Each card gets marked Holds / Shaky / Collapsed. Confidence is weighted by card type (claims and experiments count 3, assumptions and evidence 2) times how high it climbed. Deck-dwellers drag the score down. ≥70% holds, 40–69% shaky, below that collapses — but a collapsed load-bearing card forces a collapse verdict regardless of the number.

**Receipt** — "Print receipt" generates a plain-text thermal-printer-style record: plan, timestamp, every card with rung/status/challenge answers, and the verdict. Copy uses the clipboard API with a select-and-copy fallback; download builds a Blob at runtime (no URL literals) and names the file after your plan slug.

Delete is two-tap confirm via toast instead of `confirm()`, and it respects reduced-motion. State is in-memory only — the receipt is your persistence, by design.
steps.response_summary: Claude returned the first complete one-file Claim Ladder artifact.
steps.notes: Preserved exact first artifact. Functional and viewport checks passed, but static verification found document.execCommand.

steps.title: Remove the deprecated clipboard fallback
steps.prompt_exact: I tested the saved file and found one concrete safety issue: the clipboard fallback still calls document.execCommand, and our public artifact verifier rejects that deprecated token. Remove document.execCommand entirely; use navigator.clipboard when available and otherwise reveal and select a plain textarea so I can copy manually. Keep the ladder, scoring, receipt, download, offline behavior, and current design unchanged, then return the complete updated self-contained HTML file.
steps.response_exact:
Fixed. `document.execCommand` is gone entirely — zero occurrences in the file.

The copy flow is now: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` when available; if it's missing or the promise rejects, a styled textarea reveals below the receipt buttons, pre-filled with the receipt, auto-focused and selected, with a label and toast telling you to press Ctrl+C / Cmd+C. Printing a fresh receipt or a successful clipboard copy hides it again so stale text never lingers.

Everything else is untouched — ladder, challenges, scoring, load-bearing collapse rule, download path, offline behavior, and design. Full scanner re-run passed on all constraints including the new execCommand check, and the JS still passes `node --check`.
steps.response_summary: Claude removed document.execCommand and returned the complete corrected artifact.
steps.continuation_reason: Verification-proven defect: the first artifact used document.execCommand in its receipt-copy fallback.

comparison_basis.opening_prompt_exact: Can you build a self-contained one-file HTML game called First-Principles Claim Ladder where I test a big plan by moving claim, assumption, evidence, and experiment cards up a ladder, score whether the plan holds or collapses, and copy or download a reasoning receipt I can keep offline?
acceptance_criteria: Provide distinct claim, assumption, evidence, and experiment cards in one understandable ladder workflow.
Let the user move or classify cards and run a visible holds-versus-collapses reasoning check.
Produce a meaningful reasoning score or assessment tied to the current ladder state.
Provide a copyable or downloadable reasoning receipt that includes the experiment or next test.
Produce one complete self-contained HTML file that is immediately usable in a browser.
Operate offline with no external APIs, hosted generation, CDNs, remote fonts, scripts, stylesheets, or fragile dependencies.
Avoid unsafe HTML sinks, eval-like execution, inline event handlers, modal dialogs, and deprecated clipboard handling.
Avoid page-level horizontal overflow at 390 by 844 and at desktop width.
Keep essential controls visible, keyboard or touch reachable, and truthful about their current state.
Preserve exact prompt, response, source, and artifact-version evidence for the run.
comparison_basis.adaptive_repair_policy: Preserve and score the first real artifact. Continue only when verification proves a concrete defect or a source-capture failure; use the same source session and model; name the observed defect in ordinary language; preserve every real artifact version; stop as soon as the artifact passes; prefer no more than three total prompts and go beyond three only for a documented concrete lane reason such as a verification-proven regression, truncation, or mechanical capture failure.
comparison_basis.independence_note: Claude received the invariant brief in a fresh session and was not shown the historical implementation, screenshots, source code, or another provider's output.
